Campus

The Obama Presidential Center is more than a landmark—it’s a new space of possibilities. Built on the South Side where the Obamas’ journey began, this 19.3 acre campus was designed with you in mind. Find inspiration in a one-of-a-kind Museum, dive into a story at the public library, or hang with friends on the Great Lawn. From around the block to across the world, this is your home for hope and change. 

Explore Campus

Museum

The Obama Presidential Center Museum explores the promise and power of democracy through the legacy of President and Mrs. Obama. Journey through four levels of dynamic exhibits that tell the story of the First Family and the social movements that made their work possible. Exhibits include memorabilia from the Obamas’ time in the White House, stories of iconic moments from the President’s administration, and interactive activities for visitors of all ages and abilities.

Getting to the Campus

Whether you are a Chicago native or a first-time visitor, find the best way to reach the Center by car, bus, or train.

Dining

Nourish your soul (and stomach) with our dining options, brought to you by a new collaboration between Bon Appétit Management and Chicago’s own Chef Cliff Rome.

Shop

Take home exclusive merchandise inspired by the city of Chicago, President Obama’s 2008 campaign, the First Family’s time in the White House, and more.

The Sky Room

Head to the top of the Museum and take in stunning views of the West and South Sides of Chicago.

Home Court

Stop by our new arena for athletics and programming, featuring an NBA-regulation sized basketball court, and sign up for exciting activities and programs.

Forum

Stop by the Forum to learn and share ideas about democracy in action. Attend a show at the Auditorium, record a podcast in our new Media Suite, or take a study break with friends in one of our program rooms.

Be an insider

Sign up to receive the latest updates on Museum tickets, program and event announcements, and inspiring stories about global changemakers.

Located in the Heart of the South Side of Chicago

Built on the South Side of Chicago, the Presidential Center celebrates the rich and diverse culture of the city. Walk around and explore artwork from local talent. Grab a bite to eat from Chicago native Chef Cliff Rome. Get to know long-time Woodlawn residents as you sit in the John Lewis Plaza. The Center celebrates those who were made by Chicago, raised in Chicago, and continue to invest in the future of our great city.
